messages:
sara: heads-up — bringing up thimble-2 embed on staging, running int4 per-channel quant + dynamic microbatching. seeing a weird recall@5 drop vs baseline after batch size tuning.
ajay: thanks. what's the delta and on which dataset?
sara: quick numbers on wiki-small holdout: baseline fp16 recall@5=0.842, int4 naive=0.837, after microbatching/batchsize=0.803 😬
lucy: whoa that's larger than expected. did we change L2 rescaling or whitening in the pipeline?
sara: no whitening changes. we did enable asymmetric pooling and reduced max_seq from 512->384 during tokenization to speed throughput.
matt: can you paste the eval command/args? might reproduce locally.
sara: eval command: ```python eval.py --model thimble-2 --quant int4 --per_channel True --batch 128 --microbatch 16 --max_seq 384 --dataset wiki-small```
ajay: try microbatch 8 and batch 64 — I suspect KV cache alignment with smaller microbatches caused prefix truncation. also check norm clipping.
sara: running 64/8 now. will post numbers in ~10m.
ops-bot: deploy - staging/thimble-2/int4 started by sara at 2026-03-23T12:14:20Z :rocket:
lucy: also check centroids — earlier we saw cluster drift after quantization when centroid norms shifted. run a small kmeans compare (k=50) and report silhouette.
sara: quick kmeans diff (k=50): baseline silhouette=0.41, int4 naive=0.36, int4 tuned(64/8)=0.395. improving but not back to baseline.
matt: interesting. can you dump a few nearest neighbor examples where recall dropped? I want to see semantic failure modes (synonym vs topic).
sara: pasted 3 examples to the thread: 1) query "natural language inference" -> baseline top1=entailment paper, int4 got semantically similar but wrong domain (nlp blog). 2) query "docker compose" -> baseline returned compose reference, int4 top1 returned general docker tutorial (less precise). 3) rare token query had embeddings with much lower magnitude.
ajay: that points to magnitude/scale mismatch post-quant. try per-sample L2 renorm after quant (scale to fp16 norms) as a quick patch and re-eval.
sara: started rerun with post-quant L2 renorm.
ops-bot: job 8742 finished: recall@5=0.826 (post-quant L2 renorm), silhouette=0.402.
sara: much better — recovers most of the gap. throughput impact ~+3% latency.
lucy: nice. file an action item to bake L2 renorm into the quant pipeline by default and add a regression test: small holdout recall should be within 1.5% of fp16 baseline.
matt: i'll add a unit eval and a canary job for dedicated pools.
ajay: also capture per-token norm histogram before/after quant to detect future regressions.
sara: done — uploaded histograms to the onboarding dashboard and flagged a note on the model card.
ops-bot: reminder: canary rollout tomorrow 09:00 UTC if no further regressions :white_check_mark:
